action: Position the probe high on the anterior or lateral thorax.
interpretation: Initiate the exam at the superior lung fields.

action: Hold the probe steady to identify linear artifacts.
interpretation: Visualize the hyperechoic pleural line and the horizontal reverberation artifact (A-line) located deep to the pleura.
Observe the 'shimmering' of the pleura, indicating lung sliding.

action: Identify the lateral borders of the intercostal space.
interpretation: Visualize the acoustic shadows cast by the ribs on each side of the image.

action: Slide the probe inferiorly along the thorax.
interpretation: Scan downward to visualize multiple sequential rib spaces.

action: Continue scanning while assessing for pathology.
interpretation: Confirm only normal findings are present: persistent pleural motion and A-lines.

action: Slide the probe further downward toward the abdominal-thoracic boundary.
Obtain a view of the left upper quadrant (LUQ).
interpretation: Visualize anatomical landmarks: the spleen, the hyperechoic diaphragm, the kidney, and the vertebral column (spine).

action: Trace the hyperechoic line of the spine.
interpretation: Verify that the visualization of the spine ends at the diaphragm.

action: Assess the area superior to the diaphragm for artifacts.
interpretation: Confirm the spine stops at the diaphragm (normal sign) and observe the mirror image artifact. Recognize this indicates the lung is air-filled in this area.
